request.prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

Interior of a Keel pump hall built into and around an exhausted hard-rock mine. The room is large enough for industrial water machinery, with aging pumps, thick pipes, valves, analog gauges, maintenance platforms, access doors, and patched structural supports. Older metalwork bears repeated repairs, replacement plates, welds, mineral deposits, and industrial residue. Newer biometric readers, projected procedures, distributed sensors, and a ceiling-mounted surveillance drone have been fitted onto the old machinery. A narrow maintenance route leads toward deeper legacy tunnels and a sealed section of the mine. The space should show how physical systems can be visibly old while the control layer remains sophisticated.

Must be shown, exactly as written: The setting must be Keel: worn mining and maintenance infrastructure, old copper or polymetallic hard-rock workings, pumps, industrial pipes, legacy tunnels, and connected Alpha-controlled equipment. Include at least one analog gauge beside a newer projected or networked readout, allowing the two systems to appear capable of disagreeing. Include a biometric checkpoint or access gate within the pump hall or at the tunnel entrance. The room should be physically functional, not an abandoned ruin; Keel workers keep this machinery operating long after ideal replacement.

Not established, so your choice: Exact pump design, pipe diameter, wall color, warning colors, floor material, tool storage, worker count, drone design, and projected interface layout are open. The image may include dust, condensation, dampness, oil, mineral scale, or loose repair materials, provided the hall remains readable as an operating facility. The projected procedure may contain generic technical graphics rather than legible text.

Must not appear: Do not depict a pristine laboratory, a medieval mine, or a fully automated facility with no human maintenance. Do not use oil-drilling derricks, lithium evaporation ponds, or unrelated extraction machinery as the defining equipment. Do not make every display agree perfectly with every physical gauge. Do not add a giant central AI avatar or a human operator's command throne.

The look: Close documentary industrial photography translated into graphic-novel concept art. Harsh work lights and cool projected light should strike aged brass, steel, ceramic sensor housings, damp stone, and oxidized surfaces. Keep the palette in iron gray, copper, mineral green, dust brown, and pale blue interface light. Composition should emphasize the scale of the pumps and pipes against a worker-sized passage, making the machinery feel both essential and difficult to replace.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.
